question: to the Commission Dario Tamburrano (The Left), Valentina Palmisano (The Left), Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE) Subject:
Potential clash between RED II and Italy’s rules governing incentives for renewable energy communities

In 2021, Italy transposed Directive (EU) 2018/2001 by means of Legislative Decree No 199/20211. Article 3(2)(b) of the Italian Ministry for the Environment and Energy Security’s2 2024 decree establishing the national incentive scheme for renewable energy communities (RECs) references Articles 30-32 of Legislative Decree No 199/2021, which state that an REC can include completed facilities, including those that were built before its formal establishment. Having been granted the power to lay down the operating rules governing RECs by Article 11 of the aforementioned MASE decree, GSE3 has determined that, provided that they applied for state incentives before 22 June 20244, facilities can join an REC even though they were completed and operational before the latter’s establishment as a legal entity. This means that facilities that were operational before the establishment of their respective RECs that missed the 22 June deadline are not entitled to these incentives. In the light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission not think that the GSE policy outlined above runs counter to the principles of transparency and non-discrimination enshrined in Article 21(6)(e) and Article 22(4)(i) of RED II?
Does the Commission not agree that fostering the growth of RECs (an objective of the Citizens Energy Package) requires the removal of all the administrative barriers that are hampering this process?
Supporter5

Directive (EU) 2018/2001 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 December 2018 on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources (RED II); https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv:OJ.L_.2018.328.01.0082.01.ENG&toc=OJ:L:2018:328:TOC. 2 Abbreviated to MASE. 3 The Italian Energy Services Operator. 4 GSE: 1.2.1.2 Eligible production facilities and projects – ‘The CaCer [Configurations for Renewable Energy Communities] Decree and TIAD [Consolidated Text on Collective Self-Consumption] – Operating rules governing access to collective self-consumption schemes and NRPP funding’ (16 July 2025), https://www.gse.it/documenti_site/Documenti%20GSE/Servizi%20per%20te/AUTOCONSUMO/Gruppi%20di %20autoconsumatori%20e%20comunita%20di%20energia%20rinnovabile/Regole%20e%20procedure/ALLEG ATO%201%20Regole%20Operative%20CACER.pdf. 5 This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Danilo Della Valle (The Left). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.8.2026) The Commission understands that the Honourable Members are referring to a situation in which a renewable energy source (RES) facility owned by an individual self-consumer is made available to a renewable energy community in view of entering a contract with Gestore Servici Energitici (GSE)1 to benefit from a national incentive scheme for energy sharing within renewable energy communities. However, from a general perspective, it is the Commission’s view that Article 21 (6) e) applies to self-consumers and not to renewable energy communities. Article 22 (4) i) refers to members of renewable energy communities in their role as consumers and not to members of renewable energy communities who are producers/owners of a renewable energy facility. Article 22 of the Renewable Energy Directive (RED) II lays down the obligations for Member States in relation to the promotion of renewable energy communities through rights as well as an enabling framework, including the removal of unjustified regulatory and administrative barriers to renewable energy communities. The Recommendation on supporting the development of energy communities and maximising the potential of self-consumption2 and accompanying guidance3 further describe recommended pathways to the implementation of those provisions. The Commission is working with Member States through e.g. the Concerted Action on the RED and the annual Regulatory Roundtable on energy policy for consumers to ensure that the provisions are completely and correctly transposed and facilitate selfconsumption and renewable energy communities.
1 The Italian Energy Services Operator. 2 C(2026) 2850 final. 3 SWD(2026) 126 final.
